items.a: WordByWord is a reading assistant for language learners and anyone reading websites in another language, on iPhone and iPad. Open a page in its built-in browser, swipe right on a paragraph to insert the translation below it, and double-tap a word to see what it means in that sentence. It is made by an independent developer, Jinlong. [More about WordByWord](@about)

items.q: Can WordByWord translate a whole web page at once?
items.a: No. WordByWord translates the paragraph you swipe and inserts the translation right below it; the rest of the page stays in the original language. You can show translations paragraph by paragraph or sentence by sentence (or let Auto decide), and choose whether they appear straight away or only when you tap.

items.q: Does it work in Safari or inside other apps?
items.a: No. WordByWord is not a Safari extension and does not add a translate button to other apps. It has its own browser with tabs and bookmarks: type a web address or search, then swipe to translate there.

Not in the literal sense. Translating one word at a time often misses the meaning, so WordByWord translates whole sentences or paragraphs and explains single words only when you double-tap them — in the context of the sentence they are in.

items.q: Can I read X (Twitter) with WordByWord?
items.a: Yes. Open x.com in the built-in browser and sign in, then swipe right on a post to see its translation underneath, and double-tap a word to look it up (not available in Chinese, Japanese or Korean posts). This works with the X website inside WordByWord, not with the X app.

The app is available in {uiLanguages} languages and translates into {targetLanguages}, including Simplified and Traditional Chinese and both US and UK English. The page language is English by default; WordByWord detects the language you are reading and updates it, and you can also change it by hand. Some features depend on that language: double-tap lookup does not work on Chinese, Japanese or Korean text, and Chunk Extraction and Action Flow work on English only.

items.q: Is WordByWord free? What are the daily limits?
items.a: Yes. WordByWord is free to download and use, with daily limits. The free plan includes, per day, {quota.cloudSwipe.free} swipe translations with the cloud engine, {quota.localSwipe.free} with the local engine, {quota.lookup.free} double-tap lookups, {quota.chunks.free} Chunk Extractions, {quota.actionFlow.free} Action Flows and {quota.syntax.free} AI syntax explanations; iOS voices have no daily limit. **WordByWord Plus** is a monthly subscription ({plus.priceUS} in the US; local prices are shown in the App Store) that raises these limits.

items.q: Which translation engine does it use?
items.a: You choose. The cloud translation engine is currently backed by Azure and Google translation services. The local engine uses the translation built into iOS; the first time, iOS may need to download language resources. If you run out of cloud translations for the day, switch to the local engine and retry. Word explanations, syntax analysis and AI Read use AI services in the cloud.

items.q: Do I need an account to use WordByWord?
items.a: No. WordByWord works without signing up. You only sign in to websites such as x.com inside its built-in browser, as you would in any browser. A WordByWord Plus subscription belongs to your Apple Account, not to a WordByWord account.

items.q: How do I get WordByWord Plus back on a new iPhone or iPad?
items.a: Use the same Apple Account on the new device. In WordByWord’s settings, tap Upgrade Now, then Restore Purchase. To change or cancel the subscription, use the subscription settings of your Apple Account.
No. WordByWord is available only on the App Store, for iPhone and iPad, Macs with Apple silicon and Apple Vision Pro.

items.q: I’m learning English. Is SurfEnglish worth trying too?
items.a: Keep using WordByWord for the pages and X posts you choose, in English or any other language. If you would also like daily English news sorted by level ({se.levels}) and games that review the sentences and words you have saved, SurfEnglish, from the same developer, adds that with the same swipe and double-tap. The two apps work side by side. [SurfEnglish website](@se-site)

items.q: Does WordByWord work on iPad, Mac or a desktop browser?
items.a: WordByWord runs on iPhone and iPad with {minOS} or later, and from the App Store also on Macs with Apple silicon ({minMacOS} or later) and on Apple Vision Pro. There is no version for desktop browsers yet; a Chrome extension from the same developer is in preparation — see the [Chrome extension page](@chrome).
items.aExtLive: WordByWord runs on iPhone and iPad with {minOS} or later, and from the App Store also on Macs with Apple silicon ({minMacOS} or later) and on Apple Vision Pro. For Chrome on a computer there is a separate extension from the same developer, [WordByWord Translate for Chrome](@chrome). Install it only from the link on that page.

meta.title: About WordByWord — Bilingual Web Reader for iPhone & iPad
meta.description: Official facts about WordByWord, the iPhone and iPad reading assistant for language learners: features, price, who makes it, and why it is not WordByWord.io.

about.lede: **WordByWord is a reading assistant for language learners on iPhone and iPad.** Open any website in its built-in browser, swipe right on a paragraph, and the translation is inserted below the original — paragraph by paragraph or sentence by sentence. Double-tap a word to see an AI explanation of what it means in that sentence.

sections.title: Why WordByWord exists
sections.text: Learning a language by reading real websites usually means copying text into a translator, losing your place, and forgetting what the original said. WordByWord keeps both on the same screen. You decide which paragraph to translate, the translation sits right under it, and the words you are unsure about can be explained without leaving the page.

sections.title: How it works
steps: Open a page in the built-in browser: type an address or search, with tabs and bookmarks for the sites you read.
Swipe right on a paragraph. The translation is inserted below it — as one paragraph, sentence by sentence, or split automatically.
Double-tap a word. WordByWord reads the sentence, checks for phrases first, and explains what the word means there; More Definitions opens the full entry.
sections.text: On English pages you can also run Chunk Extraction and Action Flow on a translated sentence. On any page you can ask for an AI syntax explanation and listen with an AI voice or the iOS voices.

sections.title: What WordByWord does not do
sections.text: It does not translate a whole page in one tap, and it is not a Safari extension or a share extension: translation happens inside its own browser. Double-tap lookup is not available for Chinese, Japanese or Korean source text, and Chunk Extraction and Action Flow work on English only.

sections.title: About the name
sections.text: WordByWord is sometimes written “Word by Word” and is listed as “WordByWord Translate” on the US App Store. It is not a literal word-for-word translator: it translates sentences and paragraphs, and explains single words in context.

disambiguation.title: Not to be confused with
disambiguation.text: WordByWord (word-by-word.app) is not related to **WordByWord.io** or its browser extensions, to the Chrome Web Store extension “WordByWord – Vocabulary Highlighter”, to Quran or Bible word-by-word apps, or to books titled *Word by Word*. The only official WordByWord app is the one from the developer of this site: [WordByWord on the App Store](@appstore-dev).

languages.title: Languages
languages.text: Translates into {ext.targetLanguages} languages: Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean and Spanish. The language of the page is detected automatically. The extension’s menus are available in English, Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese.

faq.q: How do I translate a paragraph?
faq.a: Hover the mouse over the paragraph and press Shift. The translation is inserted below the original. You can change the key in the extension’s settings.

faq.q: How do I see what a word means?
faq.a: Hover over the word and press Control. A card shows the meaning that fits the sentence, with part of speech, base form and the phrase it belongs to. You can also turn on double-click lookup.

faq.q: Which languages can it translate into?
faq.a: {ext.targetLanguages}: Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean and Spanish. The iPhone app supports more ({targetLanguages}).

faq.q: Which browsers does it work in?
faq.a: Chrome and Microsoft Edge. Cloud translation works without extra setup; the on-device model needs version {ext.minChrome} or later and may need to download first.

faq.q: Is it the same as the WordByWord iPhone app?
faq.a: They are separate products from the same developer, built on the same idea: the translation goes under the original. The extension works with a mouse and keyboard in Chrome. The iPhone app has its own browser, swipe and double-tap gestures, AI voices, Action Flow and {targetLanguages} translation languages. [WordByWord for iPhone and iPad](@home)

faq.q: Is this related to WordByWord.io or “WordByWord – Vocabulary Highlighter”?
faq.a: No. Those are different products by other developers. This extension is WordByWord Translate, made by Jinlong, the developer of the WordByWord iPhone app.
